# Progress & Success Report

**Project:** Automated UML Dataset Generation from Natural-Language Requirements with Multimodal Verification for Software Design  
**Student / implementer:** Dipak Yadav  
**Paper co-author:** Yutong Zhao  
**Repository:** https://github.com/dipak5501/uml-generation-pipeline  
**Date:** 22 July 2026

---

## 1. Project summary

This work implements an end-to-end pipeline that:

1. Accepts natural-language requirements or source code  
2. Produces a technical specification  
3. Generates PlantUML for class, object, component, package, and flowchart diagrams  
4. Validates and repairs PlantUML, then renders PNG  
5. Scores the rendered diagram with a three-VLM ensemble using paper MMMU weights (**53.1 / 50.7 / 39.9**) to compute composite score **S** and majority accept/reject **A**  
6. Supports dataset gating for high-quality UML pairs  

Deliverable: FastAPI backend + Streamlit UI at  
https://github.com/dipak5501/uml-generation-pipeline

---

## 2. Training & data

| Item | Result |
|------|--------|
| Open UML corpus | 8,000 rows (5 diagram types) |
| Supplemental NL scenarios | +1,000 (19 human languages) |
| Supplemental code samples | +1,000 (20 programming languages) |
| Fine-tune set | ~12.9k training examples under `data/finetune/` |
| LoRA adapter | `mlx-community/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-4bit` → `models/uml-plantuml-lora` |
| Training | **3,000** iterations completed |

---

## 3. Multimodal scoring setup (local)

Paper VLMs and local realization:

| Paper model | Weight | Local runtime |
|-------------|-------:|---------------|
| Qwen2.5-VL-3B | 53.1 | `qwen2.5vl:3b` on Ollama **0.32.1** (`:11435`) |
| LLaMA-3.2-11B-Vision | 50.7 | `llama3.2-vision:11b` on Ollama **0.24.0** (`:11434`) |
| Aya-Vision-8B | 39.9 | Stand-in `llava:7b` on Ollama **0.24.0** (Aya not available in Ollama library) |

Dual Ollama is required because current Ollama cannot host both Qwen2.5-VL and LLaMA-3.2-Vision on one binary. Startup is automated via `scripts/ensure_ollama_dual.sh` / `make run`.

---

## 4. Results

### 4.1 Live three-VLM end-to-end reliability

**Config:** real Ollama VLMs, LoRA PlantUML generation  
**Cases:** 12 stratified runs (diagram types + multilingual + source-code)  
**Artifact:** `data/eval/live_vlm_reliability_summary.json`

| Metric | Result |
|--------|--------|
| Runs with all **3/3** VLM scorers available | **12 / 12 (100%)** |
| Per-provider availability (Qwen / LLaMA-Vision / Aya-slot) | **100%** each |
| Render success | **11 / 12 (91.7%)** |
| Mean composite **S** when render succeeded | **≈ 4.93 / 6** |
| Typical wall time | ~100–120 s per diagram |

One package diagram failed render (`render:failed`; **S = 0** per thesis gate).

### 4.2 Bulk generation / render stress test

**Config:** LoRA generation; VLM scores mocked for throughput  
**Artifact:** `data/eval/batch_report.json`

| Set | n | Success (valid UML + PNG) | Mean S (mock) |
|-----|--:|--------------------------:|--------------:|
| Multilingual NL scenarios | 1,000 | **974 (97.4%)** | 3.92 |
| Multi-language source code | 1,000 | **1,000 (100%)** | 4.26 |

Weakest NL diagram type: **object** (180/200 OK). Failures were primarily render failures.

---

## 5. System deliverables

- Full thesis stages wired in orchestration (spec → PlantUML → validate/repair → render → VLM ensemble → gate)  
- Streamlit UI: single generation, batch, artifact review with per-model scores and explanations  
- Language detection expanded for multi-language code inputs  
- Unit tests: 50 passed (1 known factory mapping regression)  

---

## 6. Limitations

1. **Aya-Vision-8B** is not available via Ollama; `llava:7b` is used as a stand-in under the same paper weight.  
2. Local Qwen + LLaMA-Vision requires **two Ollama versions/ports**.  
3. Bulk 2,000-case numbers measure generation/render success, not a full live 3-VLM pass over every case.  
4. Package/object diagrams still fail render more often than class diagrams.  
5. Full DeepSeek-R1-32B Stage-2 remains optional; on-device demos use the LoRA adapter.

---

## 7. Success statement

The implemented UML-Pipeline realizes the thesis pipeline (specification → PlantUML → render gate → MMMU-weighted ensemble **S** + majority **A**). On this workstation, live evaluation over 12 end-to-end runs achieved **100% availability of all three VLM scorers** and **91.7% render success**, with mean composite score **≈4.93** when rendering succeeded. Separately, LoRA generation/render tests on **2,000** multilingual and code inputs reached **97.4%** (NL) and **100%** (code) success.

---

## 8. Reproduce live evaluation

```bash
./scripts/run_local.sh

PYTHONPATH=. MOCK_PROVIDERS=false USE_OLLAMA=true USE_FINETUNED_CODE=true \
  python scripts/eval_live_vlm_reliability.py --runs 12
# → data/eval/live_vlm_reliability_summary.json
```

---

**Dipak Yadav**  
GitHub: [@dipak5501](https://github.com/dipak5501)
